text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia, who was reappointed on Saturday by President Liamine Zeroual, will form a coalition government to prepare local elections planned for autumn and implement economic reforms under an agreement with the International Monetary Fund ending next April.
- The Constitutional Council to announce verdicts on Tuesday on opposition complaints over June 5 parliamentary election irregularities.
- Ouyahia government line-up will likely to be a replica of the previous cabinet.

- Secular opposition parties, Socialist Forces Front and Rally for Culture and Democracy which gained 19 seats each in the newly elected National Assembly, say they will not enter a coalition government.
- The 380-member assembly holds its maiden session on Sunday to end a 35-year-long era of sole ruling party, though some deputies do not deserve their seats.
